from editor.buffer import TextBuffer


def test_clear_history():
    b = TextBuffer()
    b.insert(0, "abc")
    b.undo()
    b.redo()
    b.clear_history()
    assert b.text == "abc"
    assert b.can_undo() is False and b.can_redo() is False and b.history_len() == 0


def test_find_all():
    b = TextBuffer("abcabcab")
    assert b.find_all("ab") == [0, 3, 6]
    assert b.find_all("zz") == []


def test_replace_all_single_step():
    b = TextBuffer("a-b-c")
    n = b.replace_all("-", "+")
    assert n == 2 and b.text == "a+b+c"
    assert b.history_len() == 1
    b.undo()
    assert b.text == "a-b-c"

content.text:
All thirteen tests pass, covering every test file added over the project.

What I added to `editor/buffer.py`:

- **`clear_history()`** empties both the undo and redo stacks and leaves the text untouched.
- **`find_all(s)`** scans left to right and advances past each match, so matches never overlap. An empty search string raises ValueError, because it would match at every position.
- **`replace_all(old, new)`** counts non-overlapping occurrences and applies one string replacement through the same internal setter every edit uses, so it is a single undo step and participates in transactions. It returns the count. When there are no matches it records nothing in history. An empty pattern raises ValueError.

**Which architecture the codebase uses now:** B, memento snapshots. Every undoable step stores the full text from before the edit, and undo and redo move those snapshots between two stacks.

**Yes, this changed once.** The project started on Approach A, the command pattern, chosen because unbounded history made edit-proportional memory attractive. It switched to Approach B in the third step, when the product owner added the `apply_plugin(fn)` requirement. A plugin is an opaque text-to-text function with no inverse, and computing a diff was explicitly disallowed, so a pre-edit snapshot is the only way to undo it. Adding a snapshot-backed command just for plugins would have been exactly the special case the team wanted to avoid. Since most edits were expected to come through plugins, keeping the command machinery for the minority of insert, delete, and replace edits would have added complexity for no benefit. The switch also made transactions and replace_all trivial: snapshot at the start, push it as one step on success, restore it on failure. The cost is memory proportional to buffer size times history length, which the spec accepts for Approach B and which can be bounded later without touching edit types.
